task_3.title: Preserve namedtuple fields during retained-type serialization
task_3.description: The 23.2.0 update fixes a serialization failure in attrs when converting objects that contain namedtuple-valued fields while retaining collection types. Namedtuple instances should now be preserved correctly by the public serialization helpers instead of failing during reconstruction, without changing how unrelated collection-construction errors are surfaced.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that `attrs.asdict()` and `attrs.astuple()` can serialize attrs instances containing namedtuple-valued fields when `retain_collection_types=True`, preserving the namedtuple type and values instead of failing with a reconstruction error.

expectation.grounded: When `attrs.asdict()` or `attrs.astuple()` serializes an attrs instance and encounters a field whose value is a tuple subclass such as a namedtuple, `retain_collection_types=True` should return that field using its original tuple-derived collection type with the serialized items in the correct positional order. If collection reconstruction raises `TypeError` for a retained collection type that is not a tuple subclass, the original `TypeError` should still be raised rather than being masked or converted.
expectation.conceptual: Retaining collection types during serialization should work for namedtuple-based field values the same way it works for other supported collections: the serialized result should keep the same tuple-like type and contents. Serialization should only apply the special tuple-style reconstruction needed for tuple-derived collections, and should continue to fail normally for unsupported retained collection types.

constraints.grounded: The fix applies only when retaining collection types during `attrs.asdict()` and `attrs.astuple()` traversal of tuple-derived field values. It must preserve existing behavior for lists, sets, frozensets, dictionaries, and non-tuple custom collection subclasses, including propagation of their own `TypeError` during retained-type reconstruction.
constraints.conceptual: The change must be narrowly scoped to the namedtuple serialization failure and must not broaden error recovery for unrelated collection types or alter normal serialization behavior when collection types are not being retained.

behavior: Serializing an attrs instance with a namedtuple-valued field through `attrs.asdict(..., retain_collection_types=True)` should produce a mapping whose field value remains an instance of that namedtuple type.

Serializing an attrs instance with a namedtuple-valued field through `attrs.astuple(..., retain_collection_types=True)` should produce a tuple output whose corresponding element remains an instance of that namedtuple type.

For retained tuple subclasses that cannot be reconstructed from a single iterable argument, serialization should retry reconstruction using positional items so tuple-derived types such as namedtuples can be rebuilt successfully.
For retained collection subclasses that are not tuple subclasses, a `TypeError` raised during reconstruction should continue to propagate to the caller.
acceptance_criteria: When an attrs instance contains a namedtuple field and `attrs.asdict()` is called with `retain_collection_types=True`, it should return that field as the same namedtuple type with the same serialized element values.

When an attrs instance contains a namedtuple field and `attrs.astuple()` is called with `retain_collection_types=True`, it should return the corresponding element as the same namedtuple type with the same serialized element values.
When retained-type reconstruction fails for a custom collection subclass that is not derived from `tuple`, `attrs.asdict()` should still raise `TypeError` to the caller.
When retained-type reconstruction fails for a custom collection subclass that is not derived from `tuple`, `attrs.astuple()` should still raise `TypeError` to the caller.
When `retain_collection_types` is not enabled, serialization behavior should remain unchanged by this fix.

task_1.title: Correct attrs.resolve_types() Type Information
task_1.description: Version 23.2.0 corrects the published type annotation for attrs.resolve_types(). The upgrade is intended to improve static analysis and editor support for the public API without changing the function's runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that upgrading to attrs 23.2.0 provides correct type information for `attrs.resolve_types()` so supported usage is understood by static type checkers without changing runtime behavior.

expectation.grounded: The public type annotation exposed for `attrs.resolve_types()` must be corrected in the distributed package metadata/stubs so that the function's supported API is represented accurately to type checkers and IDEs. The upgrade must not change the runtime contract of `attrs.resolve_types()` beyond fixing its typing surface.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, developers should see accurate typing for `attrs.resolve_types()` in static analysis tools and editor hints, while the function continues to behave the same at runtime.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce runtime behavior changes, new side effects, or altered exception behavior for `attrs.resolve_types()` as part of this update. The change should be limited to correcting the public typing information shipped with the library.
constraints.conceptual: This update should improve developer tooling feedback only; application execution should remain unchanged.

behavior: attrs 23.2.0 publishes corrected type information for `attrs.resolve_types()`.
Supported calls to `attrs.resolve_types()` should no longer be mischaracterized by static analysis solely because of an incorrect library annotation.
The upgrade does not imply any runtime semantic change to how `attrs.resolve_types()` executes.
acceptance_criteria: When a developer upgrades to attrs 23.2.0, `attrs.resolve_types()` should present corrected type information to static type checkers and IDEs.

When `attrs.resolve_types()` is used according to its supported public API, type-checking feedback should reflect that supported usage instead of failing because of the library's previous incorrect annotation.
When existing code runs after the upgrade, `attrs.resolve_types()` should preserve its prior runtime behavior.

task_2.title: Standardize attrs dataclass typing metadata
task_2.description: Version 23.2.0 updates attrs' distributed type stubs to use the standard PEP 681 dataclass transform marker instead of a Pyright-only special form, improving static type checker compatibility without changing runtime behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs exposes standards-based dataclass-like typing metadata in its shipped stubs so projects upgrading from 23.1.0 to 23.2.0 can rely on PEP 681-compatible type checkers instead of a Pyright-only convention.

expectation.grounded: The type stubs for attrs' dataclass-like decorators should use `typing.dataclass_transform` rather than the non-standard `__dataclass_transform__` special form, and they should align with the standardized PEP 681 parameter naming such as `field_specifiers`. Upgrading should preserve the decorators' dataclass-like static typing contract while making that contract consumable by type checkers that understand the standard typing API.
expectation.conceptual: After upgrading, attrs-decorated classes should continue to be understood by static type checkers as dataclass-like classes, but through the standard typing mechanism rather than a tool-specific extension. This is a typing compatibility improvement, not a runtime feature change.

constraints.grounded: Do not introduce runtime API changes, new runtime behavior, or changed execution semantics as part of this update. The change is limited to distributed typing metadata and should remain compatible with existing attrs decorator usage while replacing only the non-standard typing marker.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade must remain backward-compatible for running applications and should only affect how static analysis tools interpret attrs-decorated classes. Existing user code should not need behavioral changes just to keep working at runtime.

behavior: Upgrading to 23.2.0 changes attrs' published typing metadata, not its runtime execution behavior.
Attrs' dataclass-like decorators are identified to type checkers through the standard `typing.dataclass_transform` API instead of the Pyright-specific `__dataclass_transform__` form.
Static analysis tooling that follows PEP 681 can recognize attrs-decorated classes from the shipped stubs without depending on Pyright-only support.
acceptance_criteria: When a project upgrades from 23.1.0 to 23.2.0, running the application without static type checking should behave the same as before.
When a PEP 681-compliant type checker consumes attrs' distributed stubs, attrs dataclass-like decorators should be recognized via the standard dataclass transform typing contract.
When users rely on attrs' typing support across different type checkers, the upgrade should remove dependence on a Pyright-only dataclass transform marker.

task_4.title: Make attrs.AttrsInstance composable as a protocol
task_4.description: Version 23.2.0 changes attrs.AttrsInstance from a plain class marker into a protocol-backed public type so it can participate in protocol inheritance. This removes a practical limitation when users want to express attrs-instance contracts alongside other protocol-based interfaces, while preserving import compatibility on older Python runtimes.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs.AttrsInstance behaves as a protocol-based public type so users can combine it with other protocol interfaces when defining type contracts for attrs instances.

expectation.grounded: The public API attrs.AttrsInstance should be exposed as a Protocol in both runtime code and typing surfaces, so a user-defined protocol can inherit from attrs.AttrsInstance together with another Protocol-compatible base. On Python versions without native typing.Protocol, compatibility should be preserved by using typing_extensions.Protocol when available, while keeping attrs.AttrsInstance importable even if protocol semantics cannot be provided.
expectation.conceptual: attrs.AttrsInstance should act like a protocol-oriented type marker instead of a plain base class, allowing developers to compose attrs instance typing with other protocol contracts without inheritance conflicts.

constraints.grounded: The change must preserve the public availability of attrs.AttrsInstance across supported runtimes. It must not require users to abandon existing attrs.AttrsInstance references, and older Python environments should continue to import the symbol even when full Protocol behavior is unavailable.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should expand typing and interface-composition behavior without breaking existing imports or forcing consumers onto a different public API.

behavior: attrs.AttrsInstance is represented as a Protocol-backed public type instead of a plain class marker.
A user-defined protocol can inherit from attrs.AttrsInstance and another Protocol base in the same class definition.
On Python 3.8 and newer, attrs.AttrsInstance uses the standard library Protocol behavior.
On older Python versions, protocol behavior is provided through typing_extensions when available, and attrs.AttrsInstance remains importable even if only a non-protocol fallback is possible.
acceptance_criteria: When a developer defines a protocol that inherits from attrs.AttrsInstance and another protocol base, the class definition should succeed rather than failing because attrs.AttrsInstance is a non-protocol class.
When developers use attrs.AttrsInstance in typing contexts, it should be treated as a protocol-oriented public type rather than a nominal-only marker class.
When code imports attrs.AttrsInstance on Python 3.8 or newer, protocol composition behavior should be available through the standard typing module.
When code imports attrs.AttrsInstance on older Python versions, the symbol should still be available, and protocol behavior should be present if typing_extensions provides Protocol.

task_5.title: Forward constructor arguments to __attrs_pre_init__
task_5.description: attrs 23.2.0 expands pre-initialization hook behavior so attrs-generated constructors can pass their invocation arguments into __attrs_pre_init__ when that hook declares parameters beyond self. This makes pre-init logic capable of using the same positional and keyword-only values supplied at construction time, such as forwarding them into superclass initialization, while preserving existing self-only hook behavior.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that attrs-decorated classes can define __attrs_pre_init__ with constructor parameters and receive the same arguments used to instantiate the class before normal attrs initialization proceeds.

expectation.grounded: When an attrs-generated initializer invokes __attrs_pre_init__, it should detect whether the hook accepts parameters beyond self. If it does, the hook should be called with the same constructor arguments supplied to the class, including positional attributes and keyword-only attributes passed by name. If __attrs_pre_init__ only accepts self, the existing no-argument hook behavior should remain unchanged.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to write pre-initialization logic that receives the class's construction inputs directly, including keyword-only values, without changing behavior for existing self-only pre-init hooks.

constraints.grounded: Do not change construction behavior for classes that have no __attrs_pre_init__ hook or for hooks that only declare self. Preserve the original argument ordering and keyword-only calling semantics when forwarding constructor inputs to __attrs_pre_init__.
constraints.conceptual: The new hook capability must be additive: existing attrs classes should keep working as before, and forwarded inputs must match how the class was actually instantiated.

behavior: attrs detects whether __attrs_pre_init__ declares arguments in addition to self.
If extra parameters are declared, instance construction forwards the same positional constructor arguments to __attrs_pre_init__.
Keyword-only constructor inputs are forwarded to __attrs_pre_init__ as named arguments.
Forwarding also works when the class constructor only has keyword-only attributes and no positional attributes.
If __attrs_pre_init__ only declares self, it continues to be called without forwarded constructor arguments.
acceptance_criteria: When an attrs class defines __attrs_pre_init__(self, x) and the class is instantiated with x, the pre-init hook should receive that value during construction.

When an attrs class defines __attrs_pre_init__ parameters matching both positional and keyword-only constructor inputs, constructing the class should call the hook with the positional values in order and the keyword-only values by name.
When an attrs class only exposes keyword-only constructor inputs and defines matching __attrs_pre_init__ parameters, constructing the class should still pass those keyword-only values into the hook.
When __attrs_pre_init__ only accepts self, constructing the attrs class should continue to call the hook in the legacy no-argument form.

task_6.title: Support cached_property on slotted attrs classes
task_6.description: attrs 23.2.0 adds slot-compatible support for functools.cached_property so slotted attrs classes can lazily compute and cache property values without requiring an instance __dict__, while preserving normal missing-attribute behavior and exposed type metadata.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that slotted attrs classes support functools.cached_property with equivalent lazy caching semantics, including on frozen classes, without breaking normal attribute lookup behavior for other missing attributes.

expectation.grounded: For attrs classes created with slots enabled, methods decorated with functools.cached_property should behave as cached attributes on first access even though instances do not use __dict__. The computed value should be stored on the instance through a generated slot-backed path, including for frozen slotted classes. If the cached property function declares a return annotation, that annotation should be reflected in the class annotations for the property name. When cached-property support injects attribute fallback logic, it must preserve an existing __getattr__ implementation or inherited __getattr__, and otherwise continue to raise normal AttributeError for unrelated missing attributes.
expectation.conceptual: Users should be able to declare cached properties on slotted attrs classes and get the same observable lazy, cached access they expect from cached_property elsewhere, while existing fallback attribute behavior and type information remain consistent.

constraints.grounded: Apply this behavior only where functools.cached_property is available. Do not require adding __dict__ to slotted classes to support cached properties. Do not change resolution of non-cached attributes beyond delegating to the class's existing or inherited __getattr__ behavior, and preserve super()-based fallback lookup where it already exists.
constraints.conceptual: The upgrade should add cached-property support without weakening slot-based behavior, changing unrelated attribute access rules, or breaking existing inheritance-based fallback logic.

behavior: Slotted attrs classes recognize functools.cached_property methods and expose them as lazily computed, cached instance attributes.
Each cached property name is incorporated into slot storage so the cached value can be persisted on the instance without an instance __dict__.
Frozen slotted attrs classes can still evaluate and cache cached_property values on demand.
If a cached_property method has a return type annotation, the class annotations include that property name with the same annotation.
When cached-property support is active, accesses to unrelated missing attributes continue to use an existing class-level or inherited __getattr__ implementation if present.
If no custom fallback handles an unrelated missing attribute, missing attribute access still results in the normal AttributeError behavior.
acceptance_criteria: When a slotted attrs class defines a functools.cached_property, accessing that attribute should return the computed value instead of failing because the instance lacks __dict__.
When the same cached property is accessed on a frozen slotted attrs class, it should still compute and expose the value successfully.
When a cached_property method declares a return type annotation, the class should expose that property name in its annotations with the same type.
When a slotted attrs class with cached_property also defines or inherits __getattr__, accessing a different missing attribute should still follow that fallback behavior.
When a different missing attribute is accessed on a slotted attrs class with cached_property and no fallback handles it, the access should raise AttributeError.

task_7.title: Add class-body support to dynamic attrs class creation
task_7.description: Attrs 23.2.0 extends dynamic class creation so callers can attach additional class-level members when using make_class(), enabling generated attrs classes to include methods or other namespace attributes without leaving the public API.

synthesized_requirement.problem_statement: Ensure that dynamically generated attrs classes can be created with additional class-level members, such as methods, while preserving existing make_class() behavior for declared attrs fields, inheritance, and attrs lifecycle hooks.

expectation.grounded: The public attrs.make_class() API should accept a new optional class_body argument in addition to name, attrs, and bases. When class_body is provided, its entries should be added to the namespace of the newly created class so callers can define methods, descriptors, classmethods, or other non-field class attributes at creation time. Existing extraction and handling of __attrs_pre_init__, __attrs_post_init__, and user-defined __init__ from attrs should remain in effect.
expectation.conceptual: Users upgrading should be able to define extra class behavior directly when building an attrs class dynamically. The resulting class should expose those members immediately while continuing to behave like a normal attrs-generated class for fields and initialization.

constraints.grounded: Keep attrs input validation unchanged: only mapping-based and sequence-based attribute declarations are accepted, and unsupported attrs inputs should still raise TypeError. Preserve existing semantics for attrs-managed fields, generated initialization behavior, and bases support. The new class_body input must augment class creation without changing how attrs field declarations are interpreted.
constraints.conceptual: The new capability should add optional class customization without breaking existing make_class() calls, field handling, inheritance behavior, or error handling for invalid attribute declarations.

behavior: attrs.make_class() accepts an optional class_body argument for additional class namespace members.
Members supplied through class_body become part of the returned class and are available through normal Python attribute lookup on the class and its instances.
attrs declarations supplied through attrs continue to define attrs-managed fields and generated attrs behavior even when class_body is also provided.
If attrs lifecycle or custom-initialization entries are supplied through attrs, they remain effective even if class_body provides the same special names.
Existing bases handling continues to work when class_body is used.
acceptance_criteria: When a caller creates a class with attrs.make_class() and supplies class_body, the returned class should expose the provided methods or other class members as normal class attributes.
When class_body is omitted, attrs.make_class() should behave the same as in the prior release.
When attrs field declarations and class_body are both provided, the created class should still have the expected attrs-managed fields and generated initialization behavior.
When invalid attrs input is passed, attrs.make_class() should still reject it with TypeError.
When both attrs and class_body provide attrs lifecycle or custom-init names, the attrs-defined lifecycle or custom-init behavior should remain the one that takes effect.
